title: Fewest Range Bumps to Reach a Target
statement:
You start with an array of zeros, the same length as target. One bump picks a contiguous range and adds 1 to every element in it.

Return the fewest bumps needed to turn the zeros into target exactly.

examples.why: Two bumps over everything up to index 1, one more on index 1 alone, and one on the last element. The 1 at index 2 is covered by the first bump only.
One bump can cover all three, but the dip to 1 means the other three layers on each side must be separate: 1 + 3 + 3. Answering max(target) = 4 is wrong.
A single bump over the whole array.

hints: Picture the target as a skyline of stacked layers. Each bump is one horizontal strip. When must a new strip start?
Walk left to right. When the height goes down, every strip you need there already started earlier and can simply end. When it goes up, the extra layers need new strips.
The answer is target[0] plus the sum of every rise target[i] − target[i−1] when it is positive.

explain.intuition:
Think of every bump as a horizontal strip in a skyline. A strip can run on as long as the height under it stays at or above its level. So moving from position i − 1 to i: if the height drops, some strips just stop, which is free. If it rises by d, those d new layers cannot come from any strip that already exists, because existing strips only reach the old height. Exactly d new bumps must start here.

Every bump starts somewhere, and at each position the number that must start there is forced. Adding them up gives both a lower bound and an achievable plan, so the greedy count is optimal. Treat the array as starting from height 0, so the first element counts as a full rise.
steps: For i from 1 to n − 1, if target[i] > target[i − 1], add the difference.
pitfalls: Returning max(target). A dip forces the layers on its two sides to be separate bumps, as in [4, 1, 4].
Adding drops as well as rises. A strip that ends costs nothing.
Forgetting the first element. It is a rise from an imaginary 0 before the array.

solutions.title: Peel off the lowest layer and split
solutions.idea: Cover a range with as many bumps as its minimum, then recurse into the pieces between the positions that are now done.

solutions.title: Count the rises
solutions.idea: New bumps must start exactly where the height rises; drops are free. Sum the positive rises, starting from 0.

followups: Return an actual list of ranges that achieves the minimum.
The array is a ring, so a bump may wrap around the end. What changes?
